title: Acyclic N10 Fails as a High Energy Density Material

species.method: HF/CC-PVDZ (primary); MP2/CC-PVDZ values also given in parentheses
species.source_note: Figure 1, p. 817 -- confirmed as a genuine minimum at HF/CC-PVDZ (paper states this explicitly)

bond_params.shape: C2h zigzag chain, 10 atoms, 9 bonds -- by inversion symmetry only 5 unique bond lengths and 4 unique angles are labeled in the figure (values read left-to-right from the terminal atom to the chain midpoint; the second half mirrors the first by the inversion center). Read directly off the published figure (Figure 1) via visual inspection, not OCR text -- re-check against the original figure before final reconstruction to confirm exact per-atom assignment order.

species.notes: Global-minimum acyclic N10 isomer studied specifically for HEDM viability (dissociation barrier to N8+N2 found too low, ~15-19 kcal/mol, paper's main conclusion -- NOT a HEDM candidate per the authors, but still a genuine confirmed minimum worth including in the stability/topology comparison). The paper ALSO reports a Cs-symmetry transition state structure (Figure 2, TS bond ~1.60 A being broken) for the N10->N8+N2 dissociation pathway -- excluded here since a TS is not a minimum, but noted as directly relevant future kinetic-stability/barrier data if that line of work is pursued (matches the 'stability cinetique' gap discussed for this project).
